correctness.rationale: Proof reconstructed from original map: log-odds coboundary fixes cycle mean; positive artanh series proves unique primitive 2-cycle above a0; derivative yields exact product multiplier; strictly convex reciprocal logistic variance gives Lambda<1. For small delta, a uniform exponential upper bound x<=exp(-a/10) and exact implicit derivative x'=-(b-x)/(g(x)+g(y)-a) control the high-coupling Floquet slope; compact/intermediate estimates exclude earlier exits. Unique negative-slope -1 crossing in (1/(2delta),2/delta) follows. Error expansion Lambda=1-2 a delta(1-2delta)+O((a+a^2delta)x) implies the claimed O(delta^-2 exp[-1/(20delta)]) boundary accuracy. Assumption a>2/[b(1-b)], delta>0 sufficiently small, and special delta=0 are separated. 421 finite exact-rational/numerical verifier checks passed; no finite test is used as an infinite proof. Nonlinear criticality and global basins remain unproved.

value.rationale: The cited game-theoretic replicator map has a known singular-looking qualitative split: at perfect symmetry its period-two attractor persists at all finite coupling, while asymmetry permits large-coupling complexity. The new theorem identifies the unique first Floquet-stability exit for an open, natural near-symmetric family and quantifies its nonuniform inverse-asymmetry divergence, including constant correction and exponential remainder. This motivated bifurcation-scale classification is neither an arbitrary parameter slice nor merely a routine recurrence computation, and informs quantitative stability of two-strategy multiplicative-weights dynamics without claiming global chaos thresholds.
